events.title: Childebert's death leaves Chlothar I king of all the Franks
events.description: Childebert died after a long illness without heirs, allowing his brother Chlothar I to reunite the Frankish kingdom, as their father Clovis I had done, and to seize Childebert's treasure. The realm was divided again among Chlothar's sons in 561.

events.title: Ghazan's Mongols defeat the Mamluks at Wadi al-Khaznadar
events.description: Near Homs, the Ilkhanate ruler Ghazan, joined by King Hethum II of Armenian Cilicia, defeated the army of the Mamluk Sultanate, the only major Mongol victory in their long conflict. Damascus surrendered soon after, but the Mongols made no lasting gains.

events.title: Mapuche warriors kill Governor Martín García Óñez de Loyola at Curalaba
events.description: In southern Chile, Mapuche warriors under Pelantaro ambushed and killed the Spanish governor Martín García Óñez de Loyola and his escort. The victory set off a general uprising that destroyed the Spanish towns south of the Biobío river.

events.title: James II flees England in the Glorious Revolution
events.description: King James II, the last Catholic monarch of England, Scotland and Ireland, fled England after William of Orange landed with a Dutch army in November. Parliament offered the crown to his daughter Mary II and her husband William III.

events.title: George Washington resigns his military command
events.description: In the Maryland State House at Annapolis, George Washington returned his commission to Congress. A victorious general giving up power voluntarily set a lasting precedent for civilian control of the military.

events.title: Jane Austen's Emma is published
events.description: John Murray published Emma, though its title page bore the date 1816. Austen's comedy of a confident young matchmaker is often judged her most accomplished novel.

events.title: Vincent van Gogh cuts off part of his ear
events.description: After a quarrel with Paul Gauguin in Arles, Vincent van Gogh cut off part of his left ear. Months later he entered the asylum at Saint-Rémy, where he painted The Starry Night.

events.title: Bell Labs demonstrates the transistor
events.description: John Bardeen and Walter Brattain showed colleagues at Bell Laboratories their point-contact transistor amplifying a signal. Transistors replaced vacuum tubes and made modern electronics possible.
